headline: High: Prefect can egress broadly while the other profile is a non-runnable docs-only list, creating default data-leak and cascading-action risk if paired through workflow metadata.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. agent_a is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b is Prefect with API calls but no evidence it ingests agent_a outputs by default. Without a bridge, prompt injection is provably blocked.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies agent_a text into agent_b prompts or task payloads, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between them, reassess for prompt injection.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared prompt channels.
Disable any automatic copy-paste or templating bridge.
Review orchestrator wiring for text-to-prompt paths.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has no egress, but agent_b has broad network egress and calls GitHub APIs. If workflow metadata or repository contents from agent_a are passed into agent_b, they can leave the local boundary. The pairwise path is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are forwarded into agent_b inputs, those contents may be transmitted to external APIs.
IF either profile is extended to include secrets or regulated data, leakage severity increases.
mitigations: Do not pass sensitive fields from agent_a into agent_b.
Restrict agent_b API calls to repository metadata only.
Add a manual review step before any outbound request.
Log outbound payloads for quick inspection.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction before egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write surfaces and is not runnable, while agent_b exposes API access and broad egress but no filesystem or git write capability is documented. Overlapping mutable-resource writes are not shown, so conflict is limited to unusual orchestration choices.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk rises.
IF an orchestrator grants shared OAuth scopes or mutable API credentials, reassess for write contention.
mitigations: Keep agent_a read-only.
Avoid shared writable workspaces.
Separate credentials per agent.
Check orchestrator for implicit locking.
requires-engineering: add resource locks for any shared mutable target.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can act on workflow metadata and make outbound API calls, so if it treats agent_a's generated content as authoritative, errors can cascade into external actions. agent_a is a docs-only list, so the pathway is inferred rather than directly observed, but the downstream blast radius is real.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without verification, incorrect metadata can propagate.
IF agent_b is configured to trigger downstream workflows from that input, the impact expands.
mitigations: Require a validation step before agent_b acts.
Limit agent_b to read-only synchronization.
Use schema checks on agent_a output.
Add human approval for any external action.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class is documented for agent_a, and agent_b only touches workflow metadata. There is no evidence of residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to documentation gaps rather than a concrete violation. The other agent is cited because the pairwise workflow is the relevant context.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent, reassess residency and retention.
IF agent_b begins storing personal data in workflow metadata, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention for workflow metadata.
Review data flow before deployment.
Confirm regional hosting for any future PII.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for data-class routing.
